statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete across 58 checks and five representative paths. Not covered: authenticated account completion, camera scanning hardware, payment/prize-claim workflows, and the separate /pwa/ shell because they require credentials, device permissions or represent a distinct scoped app.

page.notes: Public lottery result/content MPA with homepage search, result templates, archive, editorial articles and a separately scoped PWA manifest.

paths.description: Homepage and ticket-check flow: primary live-result, navigation, install prompt and search journey.
Current 1 PM result detail: representative result template and consent experience.
Old Results: representative archive/listing and date-selection journey.
Jackpot analysis: representative long-form editorial/article template and rich metadata.
Unknown route: representative HTTP failure/recovery surface.

findings.summary: The UI stays light when the user requests a dark colour scheme.
findings.evidence: The light and dark 360px screenshots are pixel-identical; computed body background remains #fff and color-scheme is normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide preference-driven dark surface/text tokens with light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme fallback.

findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matched, getAnimations() still reported three running animations lasting 2.8–3 seconds, and no reduced-motion CSS was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential animations in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) and preserve only necessary state feedback.

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences receive no dedicated adaptation.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast screenshot is visually unchanged and CSS inspection found neither prefers-contrast nor forced-colors rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations for controls, focus indicators and custom chrome; preserve system colours.

findings.summary: Page and result-state changes use abrupt swaps rather than View Transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition declarations on this MPA, while result/archive navigation is a frequent core interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin result and archive navigations with @view-transition and stable view-transition-name values.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-state-aware navigation cue.
findings.evidence: The homepage is 8,988px tall at 360px, but CSS inspection found no scroll-state container query or progress treatment; the top navigation disappears during the long result/content page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight sticky result context or scroll progress cue, using scroll-state/container queries where supported and a simple sticky fallback.

findings.summary: A consent wall obscures the primary result on a fresh visit.
findings.evidence: The 1 PM mobile screenshot is covered by a near-full-height consent interstitial before the result can be used.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep core result content available, minimise the first-layer notice, and provide an equally prominent reject path without blocking reading.

findings.summary: The consent overlay is custom chrome rather than a semantic dialog.
findings.evidence: The rendered consent UI adds multiple visible h1 elements and no native <dialog>; DOM inspection found zero dialogs/popovers.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the modal with <dialog>, one clear heading, labelled controls, focus trapping/restoration, Escape handling and a non-modal fallback.

findings.summary: Reusable cards adapt only through global layout rules, not container queries.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container/container-type despite cards and result modules being reused in several widths and templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable card/result wrappers an inline-size container and move local breakpoints to @container, retaining a basic fallback.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus can be invisible and several controls have undersized hit areas.
findings.evidence: After programmatically focusing #srch, computed outline was none and box-shadow none. The DOM probe also found visible controls as small as 14×24px.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible ring and ensure every actionable control has at least a 24×24 CSS pixel target, preferably 44×44 on touch layouts.

findings.summary: One below-fold example image lacks intrinsic dimensions and is oversized.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found ticket-example-8pm without width/height, rendered at 489px from a 1000px source, and not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width/height, responsive srcset/sizes, and loading=lazy for the below-fold ticket example.

findings.summary: The primary ticket-number field has no programmatic label.
findings.evidence: #srch has zero associated labels and no aria-label; its placeholder is the only name-like hint. Hidden sign-up/sign-in fields likewise rely on placeholders.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate visible <label> elements with all inputs; keep placeholders as examples, not labels.

findings.summary: Multiple text and control combinations fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse/axe measured ratios from 1.84:1 to 4.33:1 for Pending text, update metadata, WhatsApp/Telegram buttons, Text result and Search.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken foregrounds or backgrounds so normal text reaches 4.5:1 and large text/UI boundaries reach the applicable WCAG threshold.

findings.summary: The homepage lacks a main landmark and focus styling.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports no main landmark; the DOM has nav/aside/footer but no main, while the focused ticket input has no visible outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the unique page content in <main>, keep one visible h1, and implement consistent :focus-visible styling in DOM order.

findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff, SAMEORIGIN and Referrer-Policy are present, but Content-Security-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP (including frame-ancestors) and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; test in report-only mode first.

findings.summary: The public app surface is not controlled by a service worker.
findings.evidence: A complete manifest advertises a standalone /pwa/ app, but navigator.serviceWorker.controller was false on the audited homepage, so no offline fallback was established for this path.
findings.suggestedFix: Register a scoped service worker for the intended app entry and cache a small offline shell/result fallback; verify the declared start_url works offline.

findings.summary: Direction and logical layout support are incomplete.
findings.evidence: html lang=en-IN is present, but dir is omitted, no logical CSS properties were found, and 36 physical left/right declarations were detected.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir=ltr explicitly and migrate component spacing/positioning to logical inline/block properties so future localization and bidi text remain robust.

findings.summary: Consent choices are asymmetrical on the first layer.
findings.evidence: The fresh-visit consent layer exposes Consent and Manage options but no visible Reject/Deny equivalent, while describing sharing with 210 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer Accept and Reject with equal prominence on the first layer, use neutral wording, and make withdrawal as easy as consent.

findings.summary: Ticket-search validation is visual only and not announced.
findings.evidence: Empty submission reveals “Please enter all 5 digits”, but the input has no label/aria-describedby and the error container has no live-region semantics.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate the error with the input, set aria-invalid after interaction, and announce changes with a concise aria-live region while retaining the successful recovery path.

findings.summary: Below-fold image delivery wastes avoidable bytes/work.
findings.evidence: The image audit found one 1000px asset displayed at 489px, missing responsive sources/dimensions, plus three below-fold images without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive AVIF/WebP candidates with srcset/sizes, intrinsic dimensions and lazy loading for non-critical images.
